findings.fix: Remove or shorten the generic review heuristics the model already applies (untestable adjectives, YAGNI, thin sections, redundancy). Keep the severity mapping and the framework-specific checks such as EARS, SHALL, delta targets, [P] and [NEEDS CLARIFICATION].

findings.evidence: Three phases: **(1) resolve** framework + archetype (below), **(2) apply** the matching archetype checklist(s) plus framework conventions, **(3) output**
findings.fix: Delete the Workflow overview and the one-paragraph Phase 2 section (lines 69-72). The phase headings already show the order.

findings.evidence: **Else (fallback)**: detect the framework from path markers and read its seed profile ... classify the archetype from the profile's `doc_types` glob, or by content shape
findings.fix: Add a short ordered procedure for the fallback path: which path markers map to which framework id, what to check first, and how to spot a fused document. Each profile already carries this, but SKILL.md does not say how to choose among them.
Move this section under the Plan checklist, or name the archetype it applies to. As a standalone H2 between grounding and budget rules, it weakens the Process structure.

findings.evidence: ## Common Mistakes ... | Classifying by folder name | Use the profile's `doc_types`; folder names mislead (Spec Kit `plan.md` = design). |
findings.fix: Add a Gotchas section with environment facts that defy assumptions. For example: profile seeds resolve against the skill directory, not the CWD. A worktree root differs from the CWD. A missing TOOL_AVAILABILITY entry means the tool was not checked, not that it is absent. Several of these are now scattered through the body; collect them where the reviewer reads them first.

findings.evidence: description: Framework-aware checklist reviewer for spec-driven-development documents — ... Use when a design, spec, requirements, or plan document has been produced and needs review before the next step. Accepts a pre-resolved FRAMEWORK_PROFILE_PATH + ARCHETYPE ...
findings.fix: Review a spec-driven-development document (intent, requirements, design or plan) against the matching archetype checklist and the source framework's own rules: EARS, RFC-2119 SHALL, Given/When/Then, OpenSpec ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED deltas, Spec Kit [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] and [P], and constitution gates. Works with superpowers, OpenSpec, GitHub Spec Kit, Kiro, BMAD, GSD and generic docs/rfcs or docs/designs. Use when a spec, design doc, PRD, requirements.md, tasks.md or implementation plan needs an audit before the next step, even if the user only says 'check this plan' or 'is this design ready'. Takes FRAMEWORK_PROFILE_PATH and ARCHETYPE from the /ai-kit-spec-review orchestrator, or detects them itself. Audit only: not for fixing findings (ai-kit-spec-review-fixer), not for reviewing code diffs, and not for a document still being written in the same context.

findings.evidence: read its seed profile at `references/frameworks/<id>.md` ... if one matches
findings.fix: List the six profile ids (superpowers, openspec, spec-kit, kiro, bmad, gsd) with their path markers inline, so the fallback can pick one file without listing the directory.

findings.evidence: If nothing resolves, ask the user.
findings.fix: Default to the generic archetype checklists, classified by content shape, and record 'generic (no profile)' on the Document Type line. Ask the user only when the content shape itself is ambiguous. A headless CLI dispatch cannot ask, which contradicts the budget section.

findings.evidence: # Reviewing-Plans Skill — Test Scenarios ... Each scenario dispatches a fresh `general-purpose` Sonnet subagent. ... Results captured below in summary form.
findings.fix: Add evals/evals.json that points to the existing fixtures (design-bad.md, design-good.md, plan-bad.md). Give each case a realistic prompt, an expected_output and verifiable assertions, for example 'flags the undefined OutputSink interface as CRITICAL' and 'emits a Status: Approved line'. Include at least one framework-specific edge case, such as a Spec Kit plan.md classified as design. The prose scenario log is not machine-gradable.

findings.evidence: No evals/trigger-queries.json in the skill directory
findings.fix: Add evals/trigger-queries.json with about 20 queries: 8-10 should-trigger (for example 'can you sanity-check docs/superpowers/specs/foo-design.md before I plan') and 8-10 near-miss negatives (fix these review findings, review my PR diff, write a spec for X, lint this markdown).

Add a `### LOW (optional)` heading to the Issues Found template (lines 266-278), or say that LOW findings are dropped. Right now the Plan checklist defines a LOW tier, but the output template has no place for it.
Add the `### Files Read` block to the Issues Found template, as the Approved template already does. Otherwise a reader cannot verify grounding in the report shape that matters most.
